question.problem: Given that $\operatorname{log}⁡(3x-2)=\operatorname{log}⁡(8-2x),$ what is the value of $x?$
question.worked_solution:
Since the logarithms on both sides of the equation have the same base, we can equate the arguments. This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{log}⁡(3x-2) & =\operatorname{log}⁡(8-2x) \\ 3x-2 & =8-2x \\ 5x & =10 \\ x & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

Let's now check for extraneous solutions by substituting back into the original equation: 

- Substituting $x=2$ back into the original equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{log}⁡(3(2)-2) & \overset{?}{=}\operatorname{log}⁡(8-2(2)) \\ \operatorname{log}⁡(4) & =\operatorname{log}⁡(4)\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $x=2$ is a valid solution.
